## Historical audit: S0083

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines and supplied character ranges. Only chunk 3 is visible; image files themselves are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal and first build — line 18, chars [0,309305), student model request/history | The explicit task was a single-photo, editable Blender/SceneAct reconstruction matching viewpoint, geometry and materials. The student's interpretation was an old metalworking shop: code grouped multiple assets including a bench, lathe, flywheels, anvil, windows, drawer and storage. These names and estimated anchors are interpretations, not independent evidence of the photograph. |
| Technical interruption and repair — line 18, chars [0,309305), embedded step 1 result and following student program | Step 1 timed out after 600 seconds with empty stdout/stderr and no usable render; the cause was not established. The student independently reduced primitives and path resolution, removed procedural material graphs and requested Eevee while retaining major placements and camera. Step 2 reported `ok: true` and a usable render. Its log shows 16 samples and integrator/BVH activity despite the program's Eevee setting, so the effective engine cannot be inferred simply from the code. |
| Review and revision — line 18, chars [0,309305), embedded step 2 result and following student program | After receiving the step 2 image, the student described the bench as distant, the foreground too small and the scene too pale. Those are student judgments, not independently verified discrepancies. The revision moved the camera from (6.6, -7.7, 4.5) to (5, -4.2, 3.65), retained the 43 mm lens, reduced light powers, darkened colors, restored procedural wear and added details. Step 3 reported a usable render. |
| Selection — lines 19 [0,3950), 20 [0,374), 21 [0,58) | The final read-only student session was supplied the reference and both render images, with no tool calls recorded. The student replied `SELECT 3`; the subsequent selection event records step 3. This establishes selection, not visual superiority or a formal scene-quality score. |

**Scene checks.** The programs specify many separate object groups and constituent parts, colored finishes, and, in steps 1 and 3, procedural noise and bump. Grouping and coordinates do not prove physical contact or correct connections. Camera pose, lighting and framing were explicitly revised; no human pose is established. Neither the reference nor renders can be inspected here, so object inventory, texture fidelity, occlusion, contact, perspective and illumination remain unverified.

**Teacher input and autonomy.** No distinct teacher intervention or adoption is visible in this chunk. The task instructions and runner feedback—including the timeout and review prompts—were received; they should not be relabeled as teacher diagnosis. The student authored the repair and visual revision, but the visible record does not establish any further exploration beyond the recorded builds and selection.

**Outcome and lessons.** Two builds had formal usable-render success after an initial technical interruption; reconstruction correctness and final visual quality are unknown, not formally verified. Transferably, a simpler retry produced output after a timeout, but the responsible change is unresolved because geometry, materials and requested engine changed together. The camera and darker-material changes are task-specific hypotheses; without the images or independent measurements, their improvement remains uncertain.
